motion_rule: the cart carries him across frame every beat to 6.60, the hog carries him from 7.20; crates and ice sweep past the lens; the camera tracks alongside at his muzzle height; new shot size each beat, never wider than his muzzle filling a third of frame; ONE sideways move per beat, never up or down; the row tears past in the punch beat too
character: a lean grey wolf with a scarred muzzle and a bushy tail, riding a low flat market cart, one hind paw scooting it along, yellow eye always clear
second_characters: ONE hog docker, going right to left a step from the lens and crossing frame himself, working wide in every spoken beat, chewing his own whole fish from 4.30, carrying the wolf from 7.20 and never stopping
props: ONE white envelope with ОКЛАД written across it; ONE thin paper napkin, a big black-ink fist with the thumb poking out between two fingers drawn on it; crates of fish; a barrel
prop_continuity: the envelope is gone by 1.40; the napkin rides in his paw from 1.40 to 9.10; the hog keeps his own fish
environment: a fish row under daylight, counters and crates packed tight both sides, no far wall, no bare stretch
light_events: hard white noon off the ice, a side shaft at 3.20 blazing through the napkin and throwing the drawn fist across his muzzle

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: a dry angry male voice, biting off each word, 4.2 syllables/sec
audio.pacing: 0.00-2.85 and 2.85-4.30 each one breath, the first word starts at 0.00; after 4.30 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: his jaw opens on every syllable
audio.sfx: cart wheels, ice cracking, paper tearing, crates banging, chewing

timeline.a: the hog shoves the envelope at him and one yank tears it out of the trotter
he rips the envelope open on a straight paw, right across frame
he shakes the envelope out sideways and the napkin flaps free across frame
he snaps the napkin flat between both paws across frame, the drawn fist at the lens
he kicks off a counter as the hog hauls a crate past the lens the other way
he rakes the stretched napkin through the daylight shaft, the drawn fist burning through the paper and sliding across his muzzle
his teeth snap shut twice a step from the lens, the hog tearing a bite off his fish the other way
he crushes the napkin in his fist and drags his knuckles clattering along the crates, the hog rolling a barrel at the lens
he drops to a crouch on the rolling cart, tail tucked flat to the boards, ears back, the row tearing past
he launches off the cart across frame onto the hog back, his muzzle driving straight at the lens
he rides the hog down the row past the lens, crates whipping by, his muzzle filling frame
the hog ploughs on with him across frame, ice spraying past the lens
the crushed napkin flaps out of his fist past the lens, the two riding on

must_appear: the hog hands him the envelope at 0.00; the napkin flat between both paws at 2.15; at 3.20-4.30 the light burns the drawn fist through the paper onto his muzzle; he leaps off the cart onto the hog by 7.20 and rides him after that; every word spoken, the last by 4.30
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, night, dark scene, a static camera, a still background, standing in place, digits, a price card, scales, latin letters, slow motion, a closed jaw while speaking, a hero moving up or down the frame, multiple wolves, clothing on the wolf, the wolf walking on his own paws
